purpose: calibrate the emission rule against the only live evidence available in-sandbox: owner-quoted scores of sha256-verified public rasters
masking_authority: DrivenData staff (chrisk-dd), community thread 11516, 2026-09-16: 'Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count towards penalty terms.' https://community.drivendata.org/t/11516

fit.model: DTI ~ kappa * M_off_catalogue / (alpha * n_off_catalogue + beta * G)

verdict_note: The two-parameter catalogue-proximity model does not explain the owner-quoted live scores of 66 sha256-verified rasters (R^2 < 0, Spearman ~ 0), and no dot-field summary statistic reaches |Spearman| 0.30. Two organizer-confirmed facts explain why the evidence is this weak: (1) the public leaderboard pools only an undisclosed public subset of the region (thread 11550, 'We are not providing any information on the chunking / subsets'), so each quoted score carries chunk-luck noise we cannot model; (2) the Initial Prize Round is scored on the private subset, which no quoted score here measures. Consequence for the lane: the emission rule cannot be calibrated from live evidence, so it is set by the exact-metric marginal-inclusion bar and by the holdout-measured sigma, and no projection is written as a score.
